title: Rockenfeller wins Assen Race 2 as Rast's tyres fade
dek: Mike Rockenfeller won Race 2 at Assen for Audi Sport Team Phoenix by 4.518 seconds from Marco Wittmann, who came from last on the grid, while pole-sitter René Rast's tyres faded to fifth.

chapters.title: A wet Saturday leaves Rast ahead, with Wittmann on a high
text: Saturday's wet opener had gone to Marco Wittmann, his third win of the season, ahead of the Audis of Nico Müller and René Rast. Müller's late pit stop had briefly put him in front before Wittmann passed him on the cold-tyre outlap. The result left Rast leading the championship on 145 points, 24 clear of Müller, with Philipp Eng third on 111 and Wittmann fourth on 100.
Sunday was dry and warm, and the 37-lap race would be a very different test, with a track temperature of around 30 degrees and the heavy tyre loads Assen puts through the Hankook rubber.

chapters.title: Rast takes pole while Wittmann is stranded with a technical problem
text: Rast took pole on 1m24.849s, a lap that was good enough by 0.132 seconds after Jonathan Aberdein put his WRT Audi on the front row with 1m24.981s. Mike Rockenfeller was third on 1m25.017s for Audi Sport Team Phoenix, only a thousandth ahead of Müller, with Robin Frijns fifth on 1m25.102s and Sheldon van der Linde the best BMW in sixth on 1m25.147s.

Loïc Duval, Eng, Timo Glock and Pietro Fittipaldi completed the top ten, with Joel Eriksson 11th and Bruno Spengler 12th. Jamie Green was 13th, and the best Aston Martin was Daniel Juncadella in 14th on 1m26.087s, ahead of Paul di Resta, Ferdinand Habsburg and Jake Dennis.

Wittmann's session was a disaster less than a day after his win. A technical problem meant he never set a flying lap, and although the crew got the BMW Team RMG car going again late on, he never started a timed lap before the session ended. He lined up 18th and last.

chapters.title: Wittmann charges through from the back
text: Rast made a good start and kept the lead, with Rockenfeller up to second, while Aberdein made a poor start from the front row and was swarmed by Frijns, Duval and van der Linde before recovering to fourth. Wittmann, meanwhile, set the fastest laps in the opening stages and was in the top ten within four laps of the start.
From there he kept climbing through the field, and by the time he made his stop he had reached as high as sixth, with the front of the field still headed by Rast and Rockenfeller.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller's extra laps pay off
text: Wittmann was the first of the front-runners to stop, on lap 13, and rejoined on new tyres. Rast followed on lap 15 and Rockenfeller two laps after that, on lap 17, a gamble that gave him the freshest rubber at the point where the others' tyres began to fade.

Rockenfeller used it to hunt down Wittmann, who held him off at the De Strubben hairpin and the Geert Timmer Bocht chicane before the Audi driver found a better exit from the hairpin and passed him on the next lap. Rast, who had held a lead of just over six seconds going into the second half, saw it vanish quickly as his tyres wore, and he came in for a second set.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller wins by 4.518 seconds
text: Rockenfeller took the lead when Rast stopped again and won after 37 laps in 56m44.559s, 4.518 seconds ahead of Wittmann. Wittmann's recovery from last to second came on a one-stop strategy, although his tyres were deteriorating towards the end. Müller took third, 6.398 seconds from the winner, by getting past Aberdein, who finished fourth, 17.000 seconds behind.

Rast, recovering after his second stop, charged back to fifth, passing Frijns and Juncadella on the last lap. Frijns was sixth and Juncadella a strong seventh, the best of the Aston Martins, with di Resta eighth. Green and Fittipaldi took ninth and tenth, giving Audi seven of the top ten places. The fastest lap, a 1m27.860s, went to Eng on lap 34 as he finished 13th.
Eriksson was classified 16th with 29 laps completed, eight down, and Spengler and Dennis both stopped after 19 laps.

chapters.title: First win in two years for Rockenfeller as Müller closes on Rast
text: Rockenfeller's victory ended a wait that went back to Zandvoort in August 2017, and it was his first win of the 2019 season. He said it was wonderful to win again, called the race outstanding and explained that it had come down to keeping the tyres alive, with everyone at the limit. The rear axle was close to the edge near the end, he said, but stopping at around half distance on a one-stop plan got him to the flag without problems.

Wittmann had the other standout drive. He pushed from the start, he explained, to get everything out of the Hankook tyre and climb from 18th, and described a dry race as "uncharted territory" after the rain on Saturday. His second place gave him a double podium for the weekend, as it did Müller, who completed the Sunday podium after finishing second on Saturday.

Rast had the opposite afternoon. He had led for much of the race, but his tyres wore badly: he said he thought he had everything under control and was trying to preserve them, only for performance to drop away suddenly, and he called it frustrating and a pity for the points. Fifth place at least kept him in front at the halfway point of the season, but his lead over Müller shrank to 22 points, with Wittmann third, 40 behind.

Hankook's European motorsport director said the DTM's first visit to Assen had produced a thrilling wet race on Saturday and tough dry battles on Sunday, with the acceleration out of the corners putting heavy loads on the tyre. Seven Audis finished in the top ten of Race 2, and Juncadella's seventh place was the best result of the weekend for the Aston Martin newcomers. The DTM now heads to Brands Hatch on 10–11 August.

facts.v: Mike Rockenfeller's Race 2 win was his first in the DTM since Zandvoort in August 2017 and his first of 2019.

facts.v: Rockenfeller, Wittmann and Müller all ran one-stop strategies; Rockenfeller stopped on lap 17, Wittmann on lap 13, while Rast needed a second stop as his tyres faded.

facts.v: Marco Wittmann started 18th after a technical problem in qualifying and finished second, 4.518 seconds behind the winner.
Rast stayed ahead in the championship, but his lead over Müller shrank to 22 points, with Wittmann third, 40 behind.
